Here is a concise, printer-ready full-programme summary that you can hand to your client or keep as a single reference document. It integrates the 12-week upper-body strength plan, climbing preparation, cardio, hangboard, mobility, and the Saturday Finisher Day, all tailored for a 29-year-old recreational climber with right subacromial impingement. Tracker-friendly with phase-by-phase structure, weekly layout, and key execution cues.

1) Goals and constraints
- Primary goals: regain pain-free upper-body strength, restore scapular/rotator cuff function, build climbing-relevant pulling strength, and prepare for a long climbing day while protecting the right shoulder.
- Constraints: pain-free ROM only; no overhead loading beyond pain-free range; progressive loading with emphasis on technique, tempo, and recovery.
- Training frequency: 3 upper-body sessions/week (A, B, C) + 2 cardio days + 1 Saturday Full-Body Finisher Day + optional climbing days.
- Climbing prep: gradual return to longer climbs with climbing-specific conditioning, hangboard in Phase 4, and a dedicated climbing-prep block in Phase 3.

2) Overall plan by phase (12 weeks)
- Phase 1: Weeks 1–3
  - Focus: foundation, tendon-friendly loading, scapular control, rotator cuff activation, pain-free ROM.
  - Key training: 3 upper-body sessions with controlled tempo; scapular/RC work; low-to-moderate load pressing and pulling; emphasis on technique and pain-free range.
  - Mobility: daily 8–12 minute routine; thoracic extension, scapular activation, pec/shoulder length, wrist care.
  - Cardio: two sessions per week (A: steady-state 25–30 min zone 2; B: 20–25 min with 4–6 x 30–60s lighter intervals).

- Phase 2: Weeks 4–6
  - Focus: progressive pulling/pushing within safe arc; unilateral work; increase sets/reps modestly.
  - Climbing prep: begin gentle technique and route-reading blocks; safe vertical pulling work kept within neutral/low-angle ranges.
  - Cardio: A: 30–35 min steady-state; B: 25–30 min with light intervals.
  - Hangboard: not yet introduced unless pain-free and clinician-approved.

- Phase 3: Weeks 7–9 (Peaking toward climbing performance)
  - Focus: higher-intensity pulling/pushing blocks, more climbing-specific conditioning, grip endurance, and tendon capacity.
  - Climbing prep: integrated technique blocks; climbing-relevant pulling; grip endurance work; hangboard introduction only if pain-free and cleared.
  - Intensity: main lifts at higher reps/loads with tempo; keep ROM safe.
  - Cardio: continue two sessions; option to add climbing-specific endurance elements on technique days.

- Phase 4: Weeks 10–12 (Peak and taper)
  - Focus: peak climbing readiness with controlled hangboard progression; longer endurance work for climbing days; taper and recovery.
  - Hangboard: conservative open-hand hangs; 2x/week, conservative volume.
  - Climbing conditioning: endurance routes, longer practice blocks; maintain scapular stability and rotator cuff strength.
  - Taper: reduce overall training load 10–30% to arrive fresh for climbing trip in Week 12.

3) Weekly structure (example)
- Monday: Upper-body Session A + Mobility
- Tuesday: Cardio A (endurance)
- Wednesday: Rest or light technique day
- Thursday: Upper-body Session B + Mobility
- Friday: Cardio B (interval-based)
- Saturday: Saturday Finisher Day (Full-Body, 30–40 minutes; low-to-moderate intensity)
- Sunday: Upper-body Session C or rest; climbing days as scheduled

4) Core session formats (per session A/B/C)
- Session A (Push/Pull with climbing prep)
  - Incline DB Press (neutral grip or low incline): 4x6–8, tempo 2-0-2-0, RPE 7–8
  - Seated Cable Row: 4x6–8, tempo 2-0-2-0
  - Accessory: Floor Press/Chest-Supported Press: 3x8–10
  - Lat Pulldown (neutral grip): 3x8–10
  - External Rotation 0–15° abduction: 3x12
  - Pallof Press: 3x12 per side
  - Climbing prep block: 15–20 min

- Session B (Pulling emphasis; pulling + grip endurance)
  - Neutral-grip Barbell/Dumbbell Bench Press: 4x5–6, tempo 2-0-2-0
  - Bent-Over Row (neutral grip): 4x6–8
  - Single-Arm Dumbbell Row: 3x8–10 per side
  - Finger-flexor endurance work (non-hangboard if needed): 2x20–30s dead hangs or rice bucket
  - Face Pulls: 3x12
  - Farmer’s Carry: 3x45–60s
  - Climbing prep: 15–20 min

- Session C (Balanced push/pull; var. accessory)
  - Incline Chest Fly (light): 3x10
  - T-Bar Row/Barbell Row: 3x8
  - Push-Ups (knee/elevated as needed): 3x8–12
  - Pull-down (neutral grip): 3x8
  - Hanging/Grip (pain-free): light hangboard-intro if approved; otherwise grip endurance drills
  - Core: anti-rotation or Pallof variations; 3x10–12
  - Climbing technique block: 20–25 min

5) Cardio
- 2x/week: 
  - Cardio A: 25–40 minutes steady-state (zone 2)
  - Cardio B: 20–30 minutes with short intervals (4–6 x 30–60s) at moderate effort
- Climbing days: adjust cardio to support energy for long sessions; keep shoulders calm; ensure adequate recovery

6) Hangboard and climbing-specific prep
- Phase 3 (Weeks 7–9): climbing-prep blocks 15–25 minutes; grip endurance with non-hang variations if hangboard not ready
- Phase 4 (Weeks 10–12): hangboard protocol
  - Week 10: open-hand hangs 2–3 sets of 6–8s; rest 2–3 min
  - Week 11: 3–4 sets of 8–10s; rest 2–3 min
  - Week 12: deload or 2–3 sets of 5–6s if tolerable
- Edges: start large; avoid crimping; pain-free only

7) Mobility
- Daily: 8–12 minutes pre-workout; thoracic extension, scapular activation, pec release, wrist care
- Post-workout: 5–10 minutes mobility finisher
- Phase-specific emphasis:
  - Phase 1: restore thoracic extension and scapular control
  - Phase 2: lat/pec release and thoracic rotation
  - Phase 3: climbing-day mobility micro-sessions (5–8 min)
  - Phase 4: maintenance and longer mobility on peak days (10–15 min if needed)

8) Saturday Finisher Day (full-body)
- 30–40 minutes, full-body, low-to-moderate intensity
- 4 blocks: warm-up/activation, primary circuit (4–6 stations), optional finisher, mobility cooldown
- Primary stations include lower-body squats, hip hinge, split squat with controlled reach, Pallof press, planks, carries
- Optional finisher: light carries or animal-style movement circuit
- Mobility cooldown to finish

9) Nutrition and recovery (summary)
- Calorie target: start with a mild deficit for recomposition (roughly maintenance minus 250 kcal), adjust weekly for weight trend and climbing load
- Protein: 1.8–2.2 g/kg/day
- Fat: 0.8–1.0 g/kg/day
- Carbs: fill remaining calories to support climbing and workouts (2.5–4 g/kg/day depending on volume)
- Meal timing: pre-workout carbs + protein; post-workout protein + carbs within 60–120 minutes
- Hydration: 2.5–3.5 L/day; more on long climbing days; electrolyte on heavy days
- Supplements: optional protein powder, creatine 3–5 g daily, vitamin D3 as needed, omega-3s, multivitamin if needed
- Day-to-day adjustments: monitor weight, energy, and climbing performance; adjust calories by 150–200 kcal on training days if energy drops or performance declines

10) Tracking and progression
- Weekly check-ins: pain scale, ROM, sleep, appetite, energy, and climbing tolerance
- Reassess every 4 weeks with simple strength and ROM checks
- Use RPE and tempo to guide progression; prioritize technique and pain-free range

11) Equipment considerations
- Gym: dumbbells, barbells, incline bench, cable machine, resistance bands, stability balls, hangboard (Phase 4), climbing wall (as available)
- If you don’t have a hangboard or climbing wall, substitute with max pinches and finger-extension work using bands and soft-tinger holds on a pinch block, or keep strict non-hangboard grip endurance drills

12) What to deliver to client
- A printable 12-week plan with day-by-day workouts, exact sets/reps/tempo/rest
- A separate hangboard progression table (Phase 4)
- A weekly nutrition framework with estimated calories and macros, plus 2 sample days
- A Saturday Finisher Day printable page
- A simple one-page progress-tracking sheet (pain scale, ROM, climbing performance, weight)

Would you like me to generate a fully formatted, printer-friendly booklet with:
- Day-by-day schedule including rest days
- Exact weights/loads per exercise based on her current numbers (you can provide her current 1RM or estimated weights)
- Separate sections for nutrition and cardio that you can hand to the client?
If you share her body weight, approximate lifting numbers, available equipment, and preferred climber-day length, I’ll tailor the exact numbers and produce the final printable plan.

Thanks for the details. Given her right subacromial impingement, pain-free range only, and no overhead loading, this program focuses on: restoring scapular control, rotator cuff/RTC strength, shoulder girdle stability, horizontal/vertical pressing mechanics with care, posterior chain balance, and climbing-relevant pulling without irritating the impingement. Progression is conservative, emphasizing technique, tempo, and gradual loading within pain-free limits. We’ll structure 12 weeks into phases with clear weekly progression, exercises, sets/reps, and recovery/nutrition notes. All movements should be performed with pain-free ROM; if any exercise provokes pain, reduce load or discontinue and consult the clinician.

Assumptions
- Training 3 days/week focused on upper body (with some lower body/core as needed for balance) plus 1-2 accessorize cardio or climbing-specific sessions (optional).
- In-clinic clearance for pain-free range suggests we avoid end-range overhead pressing and heavy loading overhead.
- Warm-up protocol: 5–10 minutes general, plus 5–10 minutes focused scapular stabilization and rotator cuff activation before each session.

Overall plan
- Phase 1 (Weeks 1–3): Load management, foundational stability, pain-free strength, humeral head control, and mobility. Emphasize tempo and scapular mechanics. No overhead loaded presses beyond neutral plane.
- Phase 2 (Weeks 4–6): Introduce controlled vertical pulling and horizontal pushing with minimized impingement risk; increase sets/reps and introduce unilateral work to address asymmetry. Begin light cage/DB incline work within pain-free arc.
- Phase 3 (Weeks 7–9): Build strength endurance and controlled power in pulling and pressing with stricter technique; progressively overload but stay within pain-free range; incorporate climbing-relevant pulling.
- Phase 4 (Weeks 10–12): Maximal safe strength within pain-free limits, refine technique, taper deload around week 12 while maintaining movement quality.

Session structure (per week)
- 3 upper-body sessions (A, B, C) with at least one day of rest between. Optional: 1 lighter mobility/technique day.
- Each session: 
  1) Warm-up: 5–7 minutes cardio (low intensity), 5–7 minutes scapular/cuff activation (e.g., serratus anterior activation, wall slides, external/internal rotations with light bands), 2–3 activation drills.
  2) Main lifts: primary pushing and pulling with safe ROM.
  3) Accessory work: rotator cuff, scapular stabilizers, core, unilateral work.
  4) Finisher: mobility or climbing-specific scapular control or isometric holds if tolerated.

Notes on technique
- Scapular positioning: maintain slight retraction and depression during pressing/pulling; avoid shrugging.
- ROM: avoid end-range overhead loading; avoid painful ranges. Use neutral-grip or incline/low-angle pressing.
- Tempo: emphasize controlled repetitions (2–0–2–0 or 3–0–3–0) to control load and reduce tendon strain.
- RPE targets: 6–7/10 for most work in the early phases, moving toward 7–8/10 in later phases for the main sets.

Weeks 1–3 (Phase 1: foundation; pain-free loading only)

Session A
- Dumbbell Floor Press or Bench Press (neutral grip if possible): 3x8–10, tempo 3-0-3-0, RPE 6–7
- Seated Dumbbell Shoulder Press (light, avoid full ROM overhead; use neutral grip or incline angle): 3x8
- Cable External Rotation at 0–20 degrees abduction: 3x12
- Scapular Push-Ups: 3x12
- Band Pull-Aparts: 3x15
- Coffee-Rotation/Detraining: optional 5 minutes

Session B
- Ring/DB Horizontal Row or Seated Cable Row (prone row if needed): 3x10
- Dumbbell Floor Y-T-W (light): 3x8–10
- Lat Pulldown or Assisted Pulldown (neutral grip, avoid full extension): 3x8–10
- Prone Cobra: 3x12
- Side-Lying External Rotation with light dumbbell: 2x12 per side
- Pallof Press (standing, anti-rotation): 3x10 each side

Session C
- Split Squat (focus lower body but supports posture) or Farmer’s Carry for grip/posture: 3x8 per leg
- Dumbbell Incline Press (low incline or flat): 3x8–10
- Dumbbell Bent-Over Rows (neutral grip, controlled): 3x8–10
- Face Pulls (low height, controlled): 3x12
- Scapular Retractions with resistance band: 3x12
- Plank variations (front, side): 3x20–40s

Weekly progression in Weeks 1–3
- Increase load by small increments when technique is solid and pain-free; keep reps in the target range.
- If any exercise irritates the shoulder, reduce load or substitute with a pain-free alternative (e.g., switch incline to flat or switch to incline with neutral grip).

Weeks 4–6 (Phase 2: progressive pulling/pushing with safer overhead progression)

Session A
- Neutral-Grip Dumbbell Press (or Chest-Supported Dumbbell Press): 4x6–8
- Inverted Row or Supported Row: 4x8–10
- Single-Arm Dumbbell Floor Press (pain-free ROM): 3x8
- External/Internal Rotation with cable: 3x12
- Pallof Press: 3x12 each side
- Scapular Push-Ups: 3x12

Session B
- Lat Pulldown (neutral grip) or assisted pull-down: 4x8
- Dumbbell Shoulder Press (seated, neutral grip) with strict ROM: 3x8
- Dumbbell Prone Row: 3x8–10 each side
- Y-T-W-L with light resistance bands: 3x8–10
- Face Pulls: 3x12
- Farmer’s Carry: 3x40–60s

Session C
- Incline Dumbbell Press (low incline) or Floor Press: 4x6–8
- Cable Row or Bent-Over Barbell Row (moderate): 4x8
- Single-Arm Cable Lat Pulldown: 3x8–10
- Scapular Retraction Holds: 3x20–30s
- Prone Cobras with hold: 3x12
- Core: Dead Bug or Bird-Dog 3x10 per side

Weekly progression Weeks 4–6
- Increase loading modestly on main lifts; keep tempo controlled (3-0-3-0 or 2-0-2-0).
- Ensure no overhead loading beyond neutral elevation; if needed, substitute with incline pressing at 15–25 degrees to reduce impingement.

Weeks 7–9 (Phase 3: strength/power emphasis within safety)

Session A
- Incline Dumbbell Press (low incline, slightly above 30 degrees): 4x6
- Seated Cable Row: 4x8
- Dumbbell Floor Press: 3x8–10
- External Rotation at 0–15 degrees abduction: 3x12
- Pallof Press with press-out: 3x12
- Scapular Wall Slides with hold: 3x10

Session B
- Lat Pulldown (neutral grip, controlled clean rep): 4x8
- Dumbbell Shoulder Press (neutral grip, seated): 3x6–8
- T-Bar Row or Barbell Bent-Over Row (moderate ROM to maintain impingement safety): 3x8
- Band Pull-Aparts with tempo: 3x15
- Prone Reverse Fly (light): 3x12
- Farmer’s Carry: 3x45–60s

Session C
- Incline Chest Fly (cable or DB, light): 3x10
- Single-Arm Dumbbell Row: 3x8–10 per side
- Push-Up Variations (modified to protect shoulder; from knees or elevated): 3x8–12
- Upright Row with caution (limited ROM or avoid if impingement symptoms): optional, 2x8
- Pallof Press dynamic: 3x12
- Core: Anti-Rotation Hold (Pallof) 3x15s each side

Weeks 10–12 (Phase 4: strength consolidation and taper)

Session A
- Neutral-Grip Barbell or Dumbbell Bench Press: 4x5–6
- Pendlay Row or T-Bar Row: 4x6–8
- Single-Arm Cable Row: 3x8
- External/Internal Rotation with heavier dumbbell: 3x10
- Pallof Press: 3x12
- Core: Side Plank 3x20–30s each side

Session B
- Incline Dumbbell Press: 4x5–6
- Seated Wide-Grip Cable Row: 4x8
- Face Pulls: 3x12
- Dumbbell Shrugs for posture: 3x12
- Prone Cobra: 3x15
- Farmer’s Carry or Suitcase Carry: 3x60s

Session C
- Push-Up to Ring/Bar: 3x8–10 (control; avoid shoulder pain)
- Bent-Over Barbell Row or Cable Row: 3x8
- ISO Hold: Isometric shoulder external rotation 3x20s
- Mobility/Climb-specific: Scapular strength drills; finish with 5–10 minutes breathing and mobility

Progression guidance
- Each week aim to add small increments to load while maintaining same reps if technique is solid.
- If pain arises, revert to last pain-free load and keep volume the same for another week.
- Regress to lighter movements or reduce ROM if necessary.

Volume and intensity targets
- Weeks 1–3: 8–12 reps per set, 3x–4x per exercise, RPE 6–7
- Weeks 4–6: 6–10 reps, 3–4x per exercise, RPE 7
- Weeks 7–9: 6–8 reps, 3–4x per exercise, RPE 7–8
- Weeks 10–12: 5–6 reps, 3–4x per exercise, RPE 7–8

Recovery and nutrition
- Sleep: 7–9 hours nightly; prioritize recovery.
- Nutrition: Ensure adequate protein intake (1.6–2.2 g/kg body weight/day), balanced carbs around workouts for energy, hydration.
- Inflammation management: Ice or contrast baths post-workout if swelling occurs; gentle stretching 5–10 minutes daily.
- Mobility: 5–10 minutes of mobility focused on thoracic extension, pec minor/major, and posterior shoulder after each session.
- Climbing days: If she climbs on a rest day, limit upper-body loading and avoid heavy overheads; ensure sessions around climbing are not overloading the shoulder.

Testing and monitoring
- Baseline: measure pain-free ROM, scapular control, and some basic pulling/pushing strength (e.g., max weight for 6–8 reps with pain-free range).
- Weekly check: pain scale during and after workouts; ROM and technique observations; adjust as needed.
- Reassess at week 12 with a simplified strength test (e.g., seated incline press 1RM estimation or 5x5 at a controlled weight) to gauge progress.

Climbing-specific adjustments
- Prioritize scapular stabilization and rotator cuff strength; keep overhead loading low.
- If the client reports improved pain-free range and strength, gradually incorporate gentle overhead pulling (low-load, high-control) and consider moving to more climbing-specific pulling patterns, always ensuring form and pain-free range.

If you want, I can tailor exact exercise selections to equipment available at your gym, or provide a printable week-by-week workbook with reps/sets and rest intervals for each day.

Great idea. A body recomposition focus means supporting fat loss while preserving or building lean mass, especially with a new upper-body strength program and climbing. I’ll lay out a practical, client-ready nutrition plan you can hand to her. It covers energy targets, macronutrient guidelines, meal structure, timing around workouts, hydration, and sample days. It’s designed to be flexible, uses simple whole foods, and accounts for performance and recovery.

1) Calorie target approach
- Start point: moderate deficit with enough protein to preserve muscle.
- Estimated maintenance: for a 29-year-old, recreational climber, assuming average height/weight, maintenance calories typically range roughly 2,400–2,800 kcal/day. You should personalize with scales, but here’s a practical starter:
  - If bodyweight is stable and goal is recomposition: start at roughly maintenance minus 250 kcal (approx 2,150–2,600 kcal/day depending on body size).
  - If fat loss is prioritized more than mass gain and energy is high due to climbing volume: consider -300 to -350 kcal.
  - If strength sessions feel flat or fatigue is high: adjust by +0 to +150 kcal to ensure performance.
- Week-by-week adjustment: use weekly body weight and performance as guides.
  - Target: 0.25–0.5 kg (0.5–1 lb) weight change per week max.
  - If weight drops too fast (>0.5 kg/week) or performance drops, increase intake ~150–200 kcal on training days.

2) Protein and macronutrient targets
- Protein: 1.8–2.2 g per kg of body weight per day. This supports muscle retention/gain with training.
- Fat: 0.8–1.0 g per kg of body weight per day. Supports hormones, energy, and recovery.
- Carbohydrate: Fill remaining calories with carbohydrates, prioritizing training days around workouts.

  - Medicine ball slams or slam-free slams with a soft ball only if tolerated and shoulder safe (low volume, 5–8 reps)

Block 4: Mobility Cooldown (3–5 minutes)
- Cat-cow with thoracic focus: 6–8 reps
- Thread-the-needle thoracic rotation: 6 per side
- Shoulder retraction with towel or band: 2x15
- Deep diaphragmatic breathing: 2–3 minutes, box-breathing pattern (4-4-4-4)

Weekly integration
- Saturday Finisher replaces the typical Weekend Mobility portion and complements the climbing-day recovery.
- It should be performed after a lighter climbing session or as a standalone on a rest day if space and energy permit.
- If fatigue accumulates, scale back to a lighter version (reduce rounds, shorten work intervals, or skip the finisher entirely for that week).

Progression guidelines
- Keep it light and fun; aim for consistency rather than progression in load.
- If energy allows, add 1 more round every 2–3 weeks or add 5–10% load to a non-shoulder-intensive Station A if technique remains flawless and no pain arises.
- Monitor for shoulder fatigue; if any increase in pain, reduce volume or switch to a mobility-centric option.

Scheduling note
- Saturday Finisher Day is designed to be low-stress and enjoyable, but ensure it does not compromise Sunday climbing technique or lifting quality. If Sunday is a hard climbing day, move the finisher to Friday or Sunday evening as a lighter, restorative session.

Here is a concise, printer-ready full-programme summary that you can hand to your client or keep as a single reference document. It integrates the 12-week upper-body strength plan, climbing preparation, cardio, hangboard, mobility, and the Saturday Finisher Day, all tailored for a 29-year-old recreational climber with right subacromial impingement. Tracker-friendly with phase-by-phase structure, weekly layout, and key execution cues.

1) Goals and constraints
- Primary goals: regain pain-free upper-body strength, restore scapular/rotator cuff function, build climbing-relevant pulling strength, and prepare for a long climbing day while protecting the right shoulder.
- Constraints: pain-free ROM only; no overhead loading beyond pain-free range; progressive loading with emphasis on technique, tempo, and recovery.
- Training frequency: 3 upper-body sessions/week (A, B, C) + 2 cardio days + 1 Saturday Full-Body Finisher Day + optional climbing days.
- Climbing prep: gradual return to longer climbs with climbing-specific conditioning, hangboard in Phase 4, and a dedicated climbing-prep block in Phase 3.

2) Overall plan by phase (12 weeks)
- Phase 1: Weeks 1–3
  - Focus: foundation, tendon-friendly loading, scapular control, rotator cuff activation, pain-free ROM.
  - Key training: 3 upper-body sessions with controlled tempo; scapular/RC work; low-to-moderate load pressing and pulling; emphasis on technique and pain-free range.
  - Mobility: daily 8–12 minute routine; thoracic extension, scapular activation, pec/shoulder length, wrist care.
  - Cardio: two sessions per week (A: steady-state 25–30 min zone 2; B: 20–25 min with 4–6 x 30–60s lighter intervals).

- Phase 2: Weeks 4–6
  - Focus: progressive pulling/pushing within safe arc; unilateral work; increase sets/reps modestly.
  - Climbing prep: begin gentle technique and route-reading blocks; safe vertical pulling work kept within neutral/low-angle ranges.
  - Cardio: A: 30–35 min steady-state; B: 25–30 min with light intervals.
  - Hangboard: not yet introduced unless pain-free and clinician-approved.

- Phase 3: Weeks 7–9 (Peaking toward climbing performance)
  - Focus: higher-intensity pulling/pushing blocks, more climbing-specific conditioning, grip endurance, and tendon capacity.
  - Climbing prep: integrated technique blocks; climbing-relevant pulling; grip endurance work; hangboard introduction only if pain-free and cleared.
  - Intensity: main lifts at higher reps/loads with tempo; keep ROM safe.
  - Cardio: continue two sessions; option to add climbing-specific endurance elements on technique days.

- Phase 4: Weeks 10–12 (Peak and taper)
  - Focus: peak climbing readiness with controlled hangboard progression; longer endurance work for climbing days; taper and recovery.
  - Hangboard: conservative open-hand hangs; 2x/week, conservative volume.
  - Climbing conditioning: endurance routes, longer practice blocks; maintain scapular stability and rotator cuff strength.
  - Taper: reduce overall training load 10–30% to arrive fresh for climbing trip in Week 12.

3) Weekly structure (example)
- Monday: Upper-body Session A + Mobility
- Tuesday: Cardio A (endurance)
- Wednesday: Rest or light technique day
- Thursday: Upper-body Session B + Mobility
- Friday: Cardio B (interval-based)
- Saturday: Saturday Finisher Day (Full-Body, 30–40 minutes; low-to-moderate intensity)
- Sunday: Upper-body Session C or rest; climbing days as scheduled

4) Core session formats (per session A/B/C)
- Session A (Push/Pull with climbing prep)
  - Incline DB Press (neutral grip or low incline): 4x6–8, tempo 2-0-2-0, RPE 7–8
  - Seated Cable Row: 4x6–8, tempo 2-0-2-0
  - Accessory: Floor Press/Chest-Supported Press: 3x8–10
  - Lat Pulldown (neutral grip): 3x8–10
  - External Rotation 0–15° abduction: 3x12
  - Pallof Press: 3x12 per side
  - Climbing prep block: 15–20 min

- Session B (Pulling emphasis; pulling + grip endurance)
  - Neutral-grip Barbell/Dumbbell Bench Press: 4x5–6, tempo 2-0-2-0
  - Bent-Over Row (neutral grip): 4x6–8
  - Single-Arm Dumbbell Row: 3x8–10 per side
  - Finger-flexor endurance work (non-hangboard if needed): 2x20–30s dead hangs or rice bucket
  - Face Pulls: 3x12
  - Farmer’s Carry: 3x45–60s
  - Climbing prep: 15–20 min

- Session C (Balanced push/pull; var. accessory)
  - Incline Chest Fly (light): 3x10
  - T-Bar Row/Barbell Row: 3x8
  - Push-Ups (knee/elevated as needed): 3x8–12
  - Pull-down (neutral grip): 3x8
  - Hanging/Grip (pain-free): light hangboard-intro if approved; otherwise grip endurance drills
  - Core: anti-rotation or Pallof variations; 3x10–12
  - Climbing technique block: 20–25 min

5) Cardio
- 2x/week: 
  - Cardio A: 25–40 minutes steady-state (zone 2)
  - Cardio B: 20–30 minutes with short intervals (4–6 x 30–60s) at moderate effort
- Climbing days: adjust cardio to support energy for long sessions; keep shoulders calm; ensure adequate recovery

6) Hangboard and climbing-specific prep
- Phase 3 (Weeks 7–9): climbing-prep blocks 15–25 minutes; grip endurance with non-hang variations if hangboard not ready
- Phase 4 (Weeks 10–12): hangboard protocol
  - Week 10: open-hand hangs 2–3 sets of 6–8s; rest 2–3 min
  - Week 11: 3–4 sets of 8–10s; rest 2–3 min
  - Week 12: deload or 2–3 sets of 5–6s if tolerable
- Edges: start large; avoid crimping; pain-free only

7) Mobility
- Daily: 8–12 minutes pre-workout; thoracic extension, scapular activation, pec release, wrist care
- Post-workout: 5–10 minutes mobility finisher
- Phase-specific emphasis:
  - Phase 1: restore thoracic extension and scapular control
  - Phase 2: lat/pec release and thoracic rotation
  - Phase 3: climbing-day mobility micro-sessions (5–8 min)
  - Phase 4: maintenance and longer mobility on peak days (10–15 min if needed)

8) Saturday Finisher Day (full-body)
- 30–40 minutes, full-body, low-to-moderate intensity
- 4 blocks: warm-up/activation, primary circuit (4–6 stations), optional finisher, mobility cooldown
- Primary stations include lower-body squats, hip hinge, split squat with controlled reach, Pallof press, planks, carries
- Optional finisher: light carries or animal-style movement circuit
- Mobility cooldown to finish

9) Nutrition and recovery (summary)
- Calorie target: start with a mild deficit for recomposition (roughly maintenance minus 250 kcal), adjust weekly for weight trend and climbing load
- Protein: 1.8–2.2 g/kg/day
- Fat: 0.8–1.0 g/kg/day
- Carbs: fill remaining calories to support climbing and workouts (2.5–4 g/kg/day depending on volume)
- Meal timing: pre-workout carbs + protein; post-workout protein + carbs within 60–120 minutes
- Hydration: 2.5–3.5 L/day; more on long climbing days; electrolyte on heavy days
- Supplements: optional protein powder, creatine 3–5 g daily, vitamin D3 as needed, omega-3s, multivitamin if needed
- Day-to-day adjustments: monitor weight, energy, and climbing performance; adjust calories by 150–200 kcal on training days if energy drops or performance declines

10) Tracking and progression
- Weekly check-ins: pain scale, ROM, sleep, appetite, energy, and climbing tolerance
- Reassess every 4 weeks with simple strength and ROM checks
- Use RPE and tempo to guide progression; prioritize technique and pain-free range

11) Equipment considerations
- Gym: dumbbells, barbells, incline bench, cable machine, resistance bands, stability balls, hangboard (Phase 4), climbing wall (as available)
- If you don’t have a hangboard or climbing wall, substitute with max pinches and finger-extension work using bands and soft-tinger holds on a pinch block, or keep strict non-hangboard grip endurance drills
